title: The Burning Choir Again
premise: In the walled city of Vespergate, magic is a hanging crime, and Wendell Ishikawa survives by stealing memories and bottling them as harmless charms. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars vanish, Wendell discovers the wards were fed by stolen memories for decades — including their own, taken when they were a child. To restore the sky, Wendell must join a ragged choir of outcasts who sing unbinding songs, confront the memory-eating thing wearing King Aldous's crown, and choose between reclaiming their lost past and giving it back to the city. In the end, Wendell dissolves their own hoarded memories into the new ward, trading a self they never knew for a family that chose them.
about_author: F. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city and now writes about the things institutions try to forget. They live quietly with two cats and an unreasonable number of unfinished manuscripts.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A routine night selling bottled memories in Vespergate's night market establishes their careful, lonely life and the city's fear of magic. When a customer recognizes a charm's feeling as her own dead mother's voice, Wendell feels the first crack of guilt. Emotional beat: comfort built on theft.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass, and every star vanishes at once. In the panic, a hooded stranger presses a blood-warm coin into Wendell's hand and says their true name — one Wendell doesn't remember ever having. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo of being known.

chapters.title: The Choir in the Cisterns
chapters.summary: Wendell follows the coin beneath the city to a hidden cistern where outcasts — a disgraced warden, a mute child, a hedge-priest — rehearse unbinding songs. Their leader, Sefa, claims Wendell's stolen memories are the keystone of the fallen wards. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging offered by strangers.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Fed
chapters.summary: Hedge-priest Anselm's POV. Through ritual memory-sharing, Wendell witnesses how the crown has harvested citizens' memories for forty years to feed the wards — and sees a child's memories labeled ISHIKAWA, W. Emotional beat: grief for a self they can't recall.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The choir infiltrates a royal audience using Wendell's charms as disguises. Up close, King Aldous is a puppet of something ancient wearing his crown like a feeding mouth; it tastes Wendell's magic and marks them. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The marked Wendell must lie low while the warden, Brava, bargains with old contacts for the crown-thing's true name. The mute child, Pip, gives Wendell a drawn picture of who they were at seven. Emotional beat: found family hardening into loyalty.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Brava's POV. The warden's former partner sells the choir out to the crown's hunters. Anselm dies holding the bell so the others can escape, his last song still humming in the bronze. Wendell learns the crown-thing offers to return their memories — for the choir's lives. Emotional beat: rage and impossible temptation.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reversed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell goes alone to the throne room and pretends to accept, letting the crown-thing pour their childhood memories back — and steals, mid-transfer, the thing's own oldest memory: its original name. Emotional beat: the thief out-thieving a god.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Full choir POV rotation. In the ruined square under starless sky, the choir sings the unbinding while Wendell speaks the crown-thing's true name. King Aldous wakes, weeping, as the parasite unravels — but the wards need feeding, and only a willing memory will do. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The New Ward
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, simple and clear-eyed. Wendell pours their reclaimed childhood into the new ward, and the stars return one by one. The choir carries Wendell home through cheering streets; Pip draws them a new family portrait. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into belonging — a self given away, a family kept.
